title: DB-010 named-street override matcher (module only): deterministic ZR 12-10 named-street/alternate-width matcher from the accepted M4-T018 capture
objective: Build the deterministic matcher module for the ZR 12-10 named-street overrides (Broadway W94-97 CD7; Allen St Rivington-Delancey CD3) and the C5-3/C6-4/C6-6 alternate-width/70-ft-connector provisions, from the accepted sha256-pinned M4-T018 snapshot capture ONLY: typed inputs (borough/CD + street name + cross-street bounds), typed tri-state outputs (matched / not-matched / indeterminate, fail-closed to indeterminate), distinct override provenance, exhaustive tests incl. boundary cross-streets. MODULE ONLY - no wiring into wide_street_live_provider.py or any consumer in this packet (wiring follows after M5-T037 lands to keep loop scopes disjoint)
business_reason: DB-010: the named-street override table has no implementation, forcing the provider to refuse exceptions attestation near those segments; the matcher is the missing capability, built loop-safe as its own module
inputs: COMMAND CWD (binding; the rules suite does NOT collect from repo root - known invocation artifact): run the first two documented commands from the services/api directory (plain `cd services/api` first; cwd persists; `cd ../..` before the modularity check, which runs from the repo root). Never chain commands onto a documented command.

CODE-GRAPH NAVIGATION BLOCK (D-066-R001; regenerated 2026-09-18 at the M5-T035 acceptance seam c759a049: 734 files, 15427 nodes, 6852 edges). Run `python tools/code_graph/query.py --no-regen impact <path>` BEFORE broad sweeps. Graph is ADVISORY - verify every material conclusion in source. This packet creates a NEW leaf module with NO consumers (wiring is a later packet, deliberately - the provider file belongs to the parallel M5-T037 lane). Its only repository input is the accepted sha256-pinned capture docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/zr-12-10.snapshot.json (M4-T018; AMENDED 3/26/2026 text with the named-street table and the C5-3/C6-4/C6-6 alternate-width + 70-ft-connector provisions). Read the snapshot; NEVER any other source; no network.

CONTRACT (binding): deterministic, typed, stdlib+existing-deps only. Inputs: borough + community district, street name, and the segment's cross-street bounds (typed, normalized). Output: a typed tri-state - MATCHED_OVERRIDE (with which provision), NOT_MATCHED, or INDETERMINATE - failing CLOSED to INDETERMINATE on any normalization miss, ambiguous bound, or input outside the table's vocabulary. Every output carries distinct override provenance: snapshot sha256, section anchor, provision id, and the matched table row verbatim. Street-name matching is exact-after-documented-normalization (case/whitespace/abbreviation rules you derive FROM THE SNAPSHOT TEXT and document); NEVER fuzzy matching, NEVER geometry inference (the CD+cross-street matcher is textual - geometric segment matching is a later, separate capability).

LEGAL BOUNDARY (binding): if the snapshot text is ambiguous about whether a boundary cross-street is inclusive or exclusive, the module returns INDETERMINATE at that boundary and your report records the ambiguity as a qualified-legal-review question (G6 queue) - never a coding assumption (D-073 item 2). D-045-R009: DRAFT posture; no compliance claims; the module docstring states it implements the capture, not legal advice.

TESTS (binding): every named row (both streets); boundary cross-streets (inclusive/exclusive/INDETERMINATE per the text); wrong borough/CD; unknown street; normalization cases; alternate-width provisions; provenance fields exact; determinism (same input twice = same output). The placeholder test file already carries one passing test - keep the suite passing at every checkpoint.
Discovery routing (D-069): out-of-scope findings go in your report. Run ruff from services/api cwd before every checkpoint. Every checkpoint carries IMPLEMENTATION. No network; no WebFetch proposals.
